note: Single-pass extraction by Claude reading the paper text; evidence references sections/figures/tables. No multi-run validation.

components.description: Normalized entropy locates trajectory-neglect outliers, which STAPO selectively optimizes

nodes.name: Sparse rewards cause trajectory neglect
nodes.description: Sparse and delayed rewards in long-horizon agent tasks cause trajectory neglect, where the agent loses focus on the task goal and interaction history at intermediate steps, producing low-quality actions.

nodes.name: Prior step-level methods optimize all steps
nodes.description: Step-level methods such as GiGPO and EMPG optimize all steps indiscriminately and lack a mechanism to locate the outlier steps caused by trajectory neglect.

nodes.name: Shannon entropy conflates complexity and confidence
nodes.description: Shannon entropy of step-level action distributions conflates inherent state complexity with agent confidence, because a high-entropy step may simply reflect a complex state with many plausible actions.

nodes.name: Normalized entropy defined
nodes.description: Normalized entropy Hn is the z-score of a step's mean token entropy within the group of actions taken at the same anchor state across sampled trajectories, which decouples state complexity from model confidence.

nodes.name: IQR outlier mask
nodes.description: Outlier steps are those whose Hn lies outside [Q1 - 1.5*IQR, Q3 + 1.5*IQR] over the training batch, so outliers are located without a manual threshold.

nodes.name: Outliers are low-quality actions
nodes.description: On ALFWorld and WebShop test sets, outlier steps (by normalized entropy) cluster at negative step-level advantage while inliers have higher advantage.

nodes.name: Outliers show weak trajectory focus
nodes.description: Outlier steps have lower trajectory attribution scores than inliers, so the model's focus on the trajectory is significantly weaker at outliers.

nodes.name: Trajectory-aware reward
nodes.description: The trajectory-aware reward is the KL divergence between the policy's action distribution under the full prompt and under a trajectory-blind prompt with goal and history masked out; higher values mean the action depends more on the trajectory.

nodes.name: Trajectory-independent penalty
nodes.description: The trajectory-independent penalty is the KL divergence between the policy and the reference policy on the masked prompt, guarding against reward hacking and mode collapse when raising the trajectory-aware reward.

nodes.name: STAPO objective
nodes.description: STAPO adds a selective term, gated by the outlier mask, of alpha times the trajectory-aware reward minus gamma times the trajectory-independent penalty to a GiGPO-style two-level (episode and step) advantage group-based RL objective.

nodes.name: STAPO wins on ALFWorld and WebShop
nodes.description: STAPO outperforms all baselines on ALFWorld and WebShop, reaching 96.9% on ALFWorld with Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and raising WebShop success from 65.0% (GiGPO) to 69.0% with Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct.

nodes.name: Normalized entropy beats Shannon entropy
nodes.description: Localizing outliers with normalized entropy beats raw Shannon entropy in the ablation (ALFWorld 92.2 vs 89.6, WebShop 69.0 vs 67.2).

nodes.name: Masking both goal and history is best
nodes.description: Masking both goal and history for the reward beats masking only history or only goal, and history-only beats goal-only, so history is more critical than goal.

nodes.name: Selective penalty beats global KL
nodes.description: Applying the penalty selectively at outlier steps beats a standard global KL penalty, and raising the global KL coefficient degrades ALFWorld from 88.3% to 84.6%.

nodes.name: STAPO reduces outlier proportion
nodes.description: Compared to GiGPO, STAPO yields trajectories with a significantly lower proportion of outlier steps, and performance is negatively correlated with outlier proportion.

nodes.name: STAPO rescues cold-start exploration
nodes.description: Training Llama3.1-8B-Instruct on WebShop gives GiGPO a flat zero success rate because no sparse outcome reward is found, while STAPO's trajectory-aware reward still provides a learning signal.

isolated_nodes.name: Gain on search QA is modest
isolated_nodes.description: On search-augmented QA, STAPO improves over GiGPO by only about 1% on average, attributed to shorter interaction horizons that naturally mitigate trajectory neglect.

isolated_nodes.name: Larger lambda helps
isolated_nodes.description: Performance improves as the IQR coefficient lambda increases from 0.0 to 3.0, and STAPO beats GiGPO at every setting including the non-selective 'All'.

isolated_nodes.name: Group-based RL is cheaper than actor-critic
isolated_nodes.description: Group-based RL methods (RLOO, GRPO, DAPO) estimate advantages from groups of samples and avoid training an independent critic, improving scalability and stability.

structural_reasoning: Trajectory neglect motivates a better uncertainty signal (normalized entropy), whose outliers are validated as low-quality, then optimized selectively; results and ablations follow.
